pitch_detail.notes: A striking crack takes tool-placed cams, but footholds are sketchy, especially leaving the shallow alcove, and a hand jam helps. The start is cruxy. Better placements show up on dirt hummocks and chockstones above, with a rest around halfway. A few more crack moves, then angle slightly left on good hooks and over a small roof to a big evergreen belay. Sustained and pumpy; cams from 0.75 to 3 fit, a 0.75 covering the last roof moves.

Directly above the tree is an obvious black corner. Thin and delicate face climbing with small, sometimes hidden protection: smallest Aliens and small nuts, then a chockstone or horn sling. Muscle through the last roof to snowy ledges, where another tree serves as the belay.

review.changed: 2 pitches, no lengths or per-pitch grades stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the crack system up the centre of the slab to a ledge and build an anchor there.
Continue up the slab on the line of least resistance to the top. Walk off to the west.

review.changed: 2 pitches; text gives no grades or lengths per pitch.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the crack system up the centre of the slab to a ledge and build an anchor there.
Traverse climber's right onto the steeper west-facing wall just right of the dihedral and overhang, then follow cracks to the top; this holds the crux. Walk off around to the west.

review.changed: 2 pitches; no grades or lengths per pitch.

pitch_detail.notes: Flakes with a little runout lead directly up to a small ledge.
Cross left, pull over the bulge and clip a fixed pin, then follow the corner to a small ledge.
Straight up slightly runout terrain to a big ledge.
Up and slightly right; several line options.
Loose choss to the top of the ridge. Descend the grassy ramp west back to the lake.

review.changed: 5 pitches with stated grades; no lengths.

pitch_detail.anchor: two fixed pieces with tat, or your own cams
pitch_detail.notes: Scramble up a couple of ledges to the one beneath the twin cracks. Climb roughly 25 feet of either the offwidth or the crack that takes fists and hands to reach a ledge, then a body-width crack for 20 feet and a ramp scramble to a good belay ledge.

Up and left onto a ledge, then back right. A decent horizontal piece goes in on positive holds before heading straight up above the belay; watch the thin flake overhead. Follow the broken crack system slightly right to the open book dihedral and belay at its bottom or top.

Up the open book, then left around downsloping flakes and a slabby layback, ending with an airy move around the corner. Rock quality is poor, so it feels spicy. Belay around the corner off a slung boulder; rope drag is heavy. A 5-inch cam protects the opening moves but is optional.

A wide crack and easy ground to the top; depending on where you stop, this can be climbed unroped. Then 4th class up and right to the path back to the road; loose rock, snow and ice may be crossed in the gully.

review.changed: 4 pitches with stated grades and lengths (ft to m).

pitch_detail.notes: Mixed terrain up to and through an ice-choked offwidth to reach the snow-filled gully above.
Easy snow to a chockstone that forms the crux; pass it on ice on either side depending on conditions.
Classic alpine snow to the start of a WI3 runnel, possibly with spicy mixed climbing to reach it, then about 100 feet of ice.
Continue up the gully through a final narrow runnel of ice and narrow snow chutes to the top.

review.changed: 4 pitches written (row stores 3); lengths only where stated.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=3; the description lays out 4 pitches.

pitch_detail.notes: The direct start crosses an easy WI2 ice shelf onto a steep snow ramp that gives access to the main flow; it can be short-pitched or soloed. For more difficulty, climb the thin ice that forms to the left and go straight up. When ice is scarce, reach the flow by climbing rock through the choke, or cross the snow ramp left and back right.

Starting at the foot of the main flow, stay left of centre past the first bulge and onto a long, gentle WI2 ramp that gives a serious calf pump. A steeper WI3 section then reaches a notch between two rock outcrops. A gentle ramp on the left leads to a protected anchor stance; the pitch uses a full 70 m rope.

Head left out of the stance through thin ice to the main flow, then steady WI3 into the notch under the final headwall. The short vertical wall to the top is WI3+, the hardest part. A v-thread works for the belay low in the notch, or use boulders at the top. The top sits in the line of avalanche and rockfall from the face above.

review.changed: 3 pitches (P2/P3 are 70 m rope lengths); rappel route described as four 70 m raps with threads and a piton anchor but not as a station list, so no table.

pitch_detail.notes: Leave Broadway and follow ramps to a big right-facing dihedral on the pillar's right flank.
Free a hand crack in a cold, slimy corner to a good stance, or add an aid move early. Pitches 2 and 3 together are about 165 feet; on a 60 m rope P1 to P3 could be done in two long leads.
More free climbing or aid in the corner, wide at the top, to the pillar's top. The anchor there is fixed with a hangerless bolt, and a bivy is possible.

Short. Start off the right end of the bivy ledge on aid with a hook move, then follow a flake with cams back left into an awkward slot that takes a big cam. Belay at fixed slings, or climb on past them. The remaining belays above can be combined as you like.
Easy route finding, a crack to the top of the section. Sling belay at fixed gear. Length approximately 145 feet, uncertain.
Thin splitter crack on RPs, a brilliant pitch and a strong crux candidate. Belay at a stance well below the Table Ledge crack. Rated variously C2+ to A3 depending on style.
Small nuts off the belay, then up to a roof under the Table Ledge crack. Belay at the roof on fixed gear or climb some of P8. Length around 100 feet, uncertain.
Go right a few feet and climb through the roof with big exposure, passing a detached flake to belay.
Keep aiding toward the top and belay on a ledge at the edge of the Diamond. Stay roped.
One more pitch is needed to reach a good place to unrope.

review.changed: 10 pitches written; lengths only where given plainly (the description calls all lengths approximate and some with question marks, those omitted). P4 grade and length left out because the text for that pitch is garbled.
review.other_findings: Description grades the route C3 with free sections to 5.10; pitch 10 is only a short pitch to a place to unrope.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the chimney system from the base to a roof made by a wedged block. Pull it using hand jams and hooks, mantel over a second small roof, then follow excellent turf up and right to the top of the first buttress, about 200 feet. A double-rope rappel from a nearby tree reaches the ground.
A short chimney cuts a steep rock band; the rock is loose at its entrance.
Juggy climbing leads up the tapering buttress to a last steep step below the trees. Walk off to the left along the ridge to a saddle, then back under the cliff, only in stable snow.

review.changed: 3 pitches; P1 is the unlabeled first lead of about 200 ft (61 m); no grades per pitch.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb to the dihedral and then up it, belaying left just past its top at a stance with good gear.
Step right and climb the depression, steepening after roughly 130 feet where a belay can be arranged.
Over the steep bit, right a little, then toward a chimney under a large dead tree, following it to the dead tree and top of the buttress.

review.changed: 3 pitches; P2 length approximate so only in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the gully as it becomes a steep chimney system past an overhang, ending at a fixed wire. Runout (R).
Straight up past a snow patch, with many variations, to below a steep wall; a sling around a big block may be found.

Climb the steep wall, cross a small snow arete, then go up and right into the obvious gully, which has a large tree on its right. Follow the snow gully to the top; a sling on a tree may mark the anchor.

review.changed: 3 pitches with stated grades and lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Up the gut of the gully to a steep step, then right to good gear and a belay below a steep corner.
A steep corner with wide stemming and good protection, belaying at a tree under the snowy bench.
Cross the snow bench, then loose ground to a left-leaning gully or chimney, ending on a mini-ridge where the route meets No. 1 Gully. Described as about 80 m of ground.
A short steep wall above the gully top, then right into a snow gully to the trees at the top.

rappel_detail.notes: Down and climber's left past the pitch 3 belay to a slung block.
Straight down to a fixed nut in the right wall of a small side gully.

rappel_detail.anchor: fixed nut on the right wall of the mini-gully
rappel_detail.notes: One last rappel to the ground.

review.changed: 4 pitches with stated grades/lengths; P3 length of about 80 m kept in notes. Rappel table from the descent in order (3 raps; the last has no length given).

pitch_detail.notes: Easy slabs and cracks reach the tip of the tooth. Work up its left side on a thin crack, then right at the roof crack. Laybacking this to the ledge is probably the crux. Place a piece to protect the follower, move right into a groove and belay. Do not place gear in the balanced rock at the far end.

Starting at the left side of the ledge, stem and shoulder awkwardly up to the corner above that faces right. An easy dihedral follows, then angle up and right on steep, positive holds and jams to an alcove for the belay.
Stem and jam awkward corners on the right, then easy scrambling to the top. The grade is uncertain.

review.changed: 3 pitches with stated lengths; P3 grade is queried (5.9?) so kept hedged.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble up to find a good belay clear of the scree. The pitch is easy and slightly grassy, with runout easy ground, and ends with a short, well-protected crux move; scramble the ledge to the foot of the next tier. Simul-climbing may be needed if you belay low, or split the pitch.
A short hand crack leads to easier ground, aiming for the right-facing corner above. Carry a nut tool to clean placements. Belay where the finger crack begins.

Finger and hand cracks to the top with plentiful gear and face holds. Best to scramble to the boulders above and belay there. A variation at 5.10+ traverses right to a leaning pillar and goes up, arcing right then back left to a thin section, with a big move left to a rail; belay in boulders above.
Wide cracks to the top, after hiking up to the next formation. Descend by hiking up and left and down the ridge between two ski runs.

review.changed: 4 pitches with stated grades and lengths; P3 variation in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Start below the broken corner systems, climbing off-vertical cracks aimed just right of the roof or overhang to the left. The belay is just right of this on a big V-shaped block, with a piton and nut anchor backed up by the block.
Trend slightly left up broken corner systems to a big ledge below a chimney.
Up the chimney to finish. From the top, go past the chockstones in the couloir, rap the route depending on gear and anchors, or hike around the ridge.

review.changed: 3 pitches; no grades or lengths per pitch. Rappelling the route is mentioned but not as a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Same as the first pitch of Beanstalk, belaying at a V notch.
Traverse right off the belay into a splitter right-facing fist corner, through chockstones and some wide climbing, to a big ledge. Bigger cams up to a #4 fit well.
Follow the off-vertical corner to the top. No fixed anchor to lower from, so walk around the back to the base.

review.changed: 3 pitches; no grades or lengths per pitch.

pitch_detail.notes: The obvious hand crack to a tree.
Traverse right to a shallow dihedral, climb it to a hand crack and go up to a tree.

Belay from the big alcove. Step left onto the face to an easy exposed arete, climb the face past a protection bolt to a finger crack and a ledge under a roof split by a hand crack. Pull the roof and follow a low-angle hand crack to the anchor.
A short hand crack leads to a crimpy rail; traverse it left, clipping a bolt, and mantel onto the ledge. Edges, a splitter finger crack, then a short wide roof with good holds.
Traverse left onto a face and climb blocky features to the top of the spire.

review.changed: 5 pitches with stated grades; bolts and anchors where stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Face into a right-facing corner then a crack to a ledge. Walk left on the ledge to below a right-angling corner.
Take the right-angling corner at 5.9, or the easy but runout face left of the ledge at about 5.7 to 5.8.
Follow the weakness up and right through ledges and corners to a headwall split by a crack system.
A mungy flake in a corner rather than the expected chimney.
Easy scramble to the summit, roughly 300 to 400 feet.

review.changed: 5 entries covering 6 pitches (pitches 3 and 4 described together as 3-4; P6 length is a 300-400 ft scramble range in notes).

pitch_detail.notes: Pass the chockstone on its left, trend up through broken ground with harder moves toward the arete, then surmount the arete with great exposure onto an angled ledge.
Straight up toward a large corner system with frozen turf and ice, over a big chockstone and up a snowy chimney.
The right-facing corner and chimney system, with two short steep cruxes and good gear.
Continue up the chimney, over a loose bulge, then an easy slope to the summit.

review.changed: 4 pitches with stated grades and lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Tips to hands splitter for about 100 feet on the left wall of the couloir, belaying on a sloping ledge.

A steep wide flake for 50 feet, then a chossy ledge traverse straight right for 30 feet. The traverse is easy but spicy; an okay #3 cam hides down and right before the final pull onto the sloping ledge.

Steep corners with surprisingly decent rock and protection. The crux is the flared roof above the Dragon's Nest, followed by hummock climbing on easier ground. A long pitch that can be broken up. It joins the South Ridge route above.

review.changed: 3 pitches with stated grades and lengths; rap is a single one-rope rappel, no table.
